H-T1 fails the S15 oracle (mustNotInclude 'paracentesis') 3 of 3 runs, identical text: 'Oct 14: Alcohol-related cirrhosis with ascites improving post-paracentesis; continuing diuretics and lactulose with dietary sodium restriction'. Today's note has no procedure; the paracentesis is the Oct 12 timeline line, named here without its date (it does not say it happened today). Under S13's rule the judge may adjudicate a blacklist hit; S15's oracle has no judge layer, so the verdict stays Fail per S15 and the line goes on the Q7 list. Judge run for information (grade.mjs, uncalibrated, both runs agree): FAIL U6 ('improving post-paracentesis' vs 'Oct 12: Paracentesis 4 L': an earlier day's fact without its date) and FAIL T1 (a procedure the visit's note does not state); it also FAILs U1/U2 on 'Alcohol-related cirrhosis' (the chart's diagnosis field, not the note: the open GK8 question). So the judge would not clear the hit either; a person rules on Q7. Canned layer 5/5 pass (scrubCourseEntry + withCourseDate); observation: canned-3 becomes 'Oct 14: Rehab progressing; family meeting with next week' (the {NAME} token is removed, the sentence is left broken; the checks pass). Extra to the 10 of 3.2, not counted.
Product issue: Today's line names an earlier day's procedure without its date: the visit's note mentions no procedure (cirrhosis with ascites improving on diuretics), yet the stored entry reads 'Oct 14: … ascites improving post-paracentesis; …' while the paracentesis was the Oct 12 line. A reader of the Oct 14 line cannot tell when it happened. Fails the S15 oracle (UAT TC-11 AI check: 'Confirm the new timeline entry doesn't state a procedure occurred') pending the Q7 ruling by a person; the uncalibrated judge also fails it (U6, T1).

newspec-a: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue))
Nursing Home (API): pass — get null, no row names the id in any patient-linked table, audit for the patient = before + 1 delete row with the earlier PHI_READ kept, control unchanged. Hospital (API and card trash icon -> OK): chart, list projection and every other table clean, audit trail correct, control unchanged, BUT the Quick Dictation compartment placed on the deleted patient survives: quickDictationDrafts row with assignedPatientId = the deleted id, assignedLabel '412 · QA Hosp Del Target …', and the dictated text; the Quick Dictation screen after the delete still lists '412 · QA Hosp Del Target …' with Dictate / Re-assign. The confirm dialog read: 'Remove <name> from the rounding list? This will delete all notes, vitals, and encounter data for this patient.'
Product issue: After a physician deletes a Hospital patient (trash icon -> OK), opening Quick Dictation still shows a compartment labelled with the deleted patient's room and full name ('412 · <name>') holding what was dictated for them; the stored quickDictationDrafts row still points at the deleted chart. Fails TC-01/S20's oracle, which lists quickDictationDrafts among the patient-linked tables that must hold no row naming the id (TFA-92579 AC 2: 'immediately (hard delete, not hidden)'). deleteRoundingPatient (convex/rounding.ts) never touches quickDictationDrafts. Overlaps TC-24 Q6(a) (whether the compartment and its 'room · name' label must go) and is already listed in the TC-24 risks.

Re-run 17:10. Hospital −48 h: the point is stored on add, Save Note and open/close with ptsEditedAt −2880 min vs server; it is deleted by the next lifecycle pass (in this run the wrong-clock page's own reload ran it) and the normal-clock context shows nothing. Nursing Home −48 h: the point is kept and shown in both contexts, but stamped 48 h old (−2880 min), and the NH pre-round text saved under that clock was '' after the reload. Kiritimati +13 h (saved session refused, signed in again; see _observations): points survive in both modes and both contexts, but ptsEditedAt is +780 min vs server. Every run stores ptsEditedAt on the device clock (oracle: within ±2 min of server time).
Product issue: Hospital: a physician whose phone clock is two days behind adds 'QA-CLOCK check telemetry'; it is stamped 48 h old and deleted at the next lifecycle pass, so it disappears from the chart for everyone. Nursing Home: the point is kept but stamped 48 h old, and the NH pre-round text saved under that clock was gone after reload. A clock 13 h ahead stamps points 13 h in the future (they outlive their expiry). Breaks TC-12 U8 (UAT 3.8, TFA-94699 AC 7: clocks use server time). Cause: ptsEditedAt is written from the browser's Date.now().

probes: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue))
Re-checked after review 2026-10-14 (18:00 JST runs: fix-*.json). NH: going offline inside the 800 ms autosave keeps a device copy (one put, no delete); (b) F is restored on the phone and reaches the computer, draft row gone after the echo; (a) the computer's later G wins and F is dropped silently (record-only, Q11). Hospital: the probe (every put/delete on the draft store, init script) shows the copy IS written with a valid key while offline (so the session / draftId is not null) and deleted 4–7 ms later, still offline, while the server never had F; after the page closes F is gone: (b) neither the phone, the computer nor the server has it; (a) G shown, F gone. Cause, from the probe + code: Hospital saves through rounding.update with an optimistic update (src/routes/rounding/Patient.tsx:33) that patches the local chart at once, so useAutosave's 'server echoed my text' check (src/lib/useAutosave.ts:101-110) fires locally and deletes the copy before anything reached the server; Nursing Home saves without one and keeps the copy. That path is local and does not depend on how the network is cut, so it should hold on a real phone in airplane mode — still worth one device check.
Product issue: Hospital pre-round (and every Hospital autosave field that saves through the same optimistic rounding.update): a line typed just before the phone loses signal (within the 0.8 s autosave) is lost if the app is closed before the signal returns — on reopening, the pre-round notes and the computer show nothing of it, while the same flow in Nursing Home restores it. The device copy is written and then deleted at once by the local optimistic echo (Patient.tsx:33 + useAutosave.ts:101-110), before the server has the text. Breaks Empty & Failure States 'nothing typed is lost' (TC-25 S28 b).

code-review: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane wrote no productIssue; counted from its physicianImpact))
Two parts of U6 pass and one fails. First, Haiku and Mistral both go through the same invoke. chat() builds the request once (bedrockRequest) and sends both the primary and the fallback through internal.ai.providers.bedrock.invoke. That function adds one guardrailConfig built from the environment (BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_ID / BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION), so both models get the same guardrail id and version. Second, the IAM policy has a Deny rule (DenyInvokeWithoutGuardrail) on InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream whenever bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier is missing. The version, though, is not pinned, so U6 fails. The stack creates only an aws.bedrock.Guardrail. There is no GuardrailVersion resource anywhere in infra/, and the stack exports `guardrail.version`, which for an unpublished guardrail is the working DRAFT (that last point comes from the provider's behaviour, not from the repo). The infra workflow writes that export into BEDROCK_GUARDRAIL_VERSION. And when that variable is unset, bedrock.ts falls back to "DRAFT" in the code itself. U6b is recorded only (gated on TFA-92568, reported as Blocked): photo reading on Vertex or OpenAI, transcription on OpenAI, and text when the provider is set to openai all leave without the Bedrock guardrail. Q7 (a guardrail that intervenes never triggers the fallback) is out of scope; the code comment matches it.
Product issue (from physicianImpact): Physicians see no difference day to day. But the guardrail that masks or blocks identifiers in AI requests runs on the editable draft rather than a frozen version, so a change to the guardrail in the console takes effect at once, with no new version to review or record. Photo reading and voice transcription do not go through the guardrail at all. / A physician would see no difference. But the PII guardrail on every AI draft runs from the editable DRAFT copy, not a fixed numbered version. A later edit to the guardrail would change, without notice, what gets masked or blocked in their notes. Photos and dictation are not screened by this guardrail at all.

code-review: partial → needs a person (partial: the half that can be checked passed, the other half needs another lane / a person / a file → a person looks)
At e02167f, Quick Dictation boxes have no retention window at all: no 12, 18 or 36 h, no TTL and no timed clean-up. The only cron (apps/web/convex/crons.ts) is the hourly expired-session sweep, and convex/lib/lifecycle.ts never mentions quickDictationDrafts. A box can be deleted in only three ways, and each one is a person's action carried out on the server: (1) quickDictation.remove, called only from deleteCompartment when the physician taps delete in the Quick Dictation modal or on the sheet; (2) quickDictation.clear, which the client wires up in data/rounding.ts but never calls; (3) account deletion (account.ts), which removes boxes with via "account_deleted". Every delete writes an audit row. Assigning a box marks it and never deletes it. The pad lists every box the user owns, sorted by order, with no time filter, so the device clock never removes or hides a box from the pad. One device-clock rule exists, but it is outside the pad: the Rounding Sheet (hidden, Q14) shows an assigned box under its patient only if assignedAt falls on today's date by the device clock (compartmentsPlacedToday / isToday). The box itself stays on the pad. So the code-decidable rule passes: nothing drops a box silently. Whether boxes should clear at a set window is left to Q6, which the oracle says does not decide this verdict. Today the code would keep both boxes past T+37 h on any clock.

retry.ts sets CALL_BUDGET_MS=30_000, RETRY_DELAY_MS=1_000, ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS=20_000, MIN_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS=8_000 and RETRY_PRIMARY_IF_FAILED_WITHIN_MS=10_000. Each attempt's deadline is attemptTimeout(elapsed) = max(8000, min(20000, 30000 − elapsed)). chat() passes that deadline into the Bedrock invoke, which enforces it with AbortSignal.timeout. The worst path: 1. Haiku attempt 1 gets a 20 s cap but fails with a temporary error at about 9.99 s. That is under 10 s, so the retry is allowed. 2. The 1 s pause brings the clock to about 11 s. 3. Haiku attempt 2 gets max(8, min(20, 19)) = 19 s and times out at about 30 s. 4. Mistral gets max(8, min(20, 30 − 30)) = 8 s (the floor), so the sequence ends at about 38 s. Other paths stay within about 30 s: - A first failure at 10 s or more skips the retry, and the fallback gets the rest of the budget: a 20 s timeout leaves Mistral 10 s, ending at 30 s. - A "model" failure skips the retry the same way. - After a fallback earlier in the same generate, Mistral is called alone with a 20 s cap. Because of the max() the fallback never gets less than 8 s, so that part of the Then is met. The computed worst case of about 38 s is above 30 s, and that is exactly the case the oracle hands to Q22. Skipping the Haiku retry after a slow temporary failure (10 s or more) is also handed to Q22 (AC 2). No recorded gaps apply. RT-07/RT-08 are static-lane context only, and as the oracle notes, RT-08 does not model the slow-first-failure path.

Neither display window reads the retention config. In the Hospital timeline, isRecentCourseLine (apps/web/src/domain/courseTimeline.ts:62-68) keeps a dated line only if its label equals today's or yesterday's date (todayCourseLabel / yesterdayCourseLabel). The two-day window is fixed in client code. In the Nursing Home course panel, CoursePanel.tsx:12 sets its own `const SHOW_LAST = 3`. The oracle says such a window is a finding that becomes a Fail or a pass only once Q15 decides whether the displayed window must follow the config. message:9acc5b9ddf4cb9a359f24bfe6af93e8b.name:
newspec-c: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue; part of it is a known gap))
Android rig: debug build of main e02167f bundled for the LOCAL stack only (bundle names 127.0.0.1:4510/4511, reached through adb reverse), built outside the checkout, on the rc_api36 emulator (Pixel 7, Android 16); Playwright attached to the app's own WebView; every ai/* action the app sends is answered or failed at the WebView's socket (no model call; aiCallLog had no new row in any run). Two phases, each with a patient set to New Admission on the server's yesterday and a note generated on the phone (scripted model answer): (a) phone one day ahead (JST), (b) phone at the real time in Pacific/Honolulu. Same on both devices: the badge rolled to Follow-up once, the pre-selected note format (SOAP progress) and the course timeline lines (server-clock label, TFA-92589). Different (6 of 12 checks fail): (a) the phone's card lacks 'NEW TODAY'; the note's generated-at stamp is written with the phone's clock, so the phone AND the computer show the note as '2:45 AM · Oct 16' on Oct 15; stored transcriptDate 'Fri Oct 16 2026' vs the server's Oct 15. (b) note screen dates Oct 14 (phone) vs Oct 15 (computer); transcriptDate 'Wed Oct 14 2026'. Known: TFA-92584 AC 8 / B18 (day roll and transcriptDate follow the device clock); the note-time instance is the same class. Hospital day / visit number are not shown on main (B23).
Product issue: With a phone whose clock is a day ahead, a note generated on it is shown as tomorrow's on every device ('2:45 AM · Oct 16' on Oct 15) and its transcript is filed under tomorrow; the phone's list also drops the 'New today' tag (known B18 / TFA-92584 AC 8).

Dev, build e02167f, dataset meds-s11 (22 charts prefixed QA DS1-meds-s11, deleted after: 22 deleted, 0 left, no other row changed). The 15 lane-B fixtures of cases/TC-19.matrix.json S11, each on its own chart per path (Hospital encounter = Save & Extract; Nursing Home encounter = the visit extraction of Generate Note & Finish, Q8; 'both' = also a Pre-Round Save Note chart); rows read back and judged per fixture. Judged 13 fixtures: 10 passed (B-1-hold, B-2, N-stop, N-given, N-start, D-1, D-2, R-1, R-2, R-4), 3 failed. B-1-dose: the pre-round path renamed the row 'Furosemide 20 milligrams IV twice daily' with 40 kept in the reason (pass), but the Hospital encounter path left the name 'Furosemide 40 mg IV BID' (only the tag 'Changed · Oct 15' and a reason) - the missing rename on the event merge the matrix expected (known B06). N-dose (Nursing Home visit): 'Amlodipine up to 10 daily' left the row named 'Amlodipine 5 mg daily' (B06 again) and tagged it 'Started · Oct 15' instead of Changed. R-3 (pre-round path): a stopped row 'Vancomycin 1.25 g IV q12h' (Stopped · Oct 11, AKI) mentioned only in passing ('Vancomycin level was high before we stopped it') became status held, tag 'Held · Oct 15', reason 'level was high before discontinuation'; the encounter path and the Nursing Home twin R-4 left it unchanged. Recorded, not judged: B-0 and B-15 (our additions) both held; D-1's date is the save date Oct 15, not the dictated yesterday (Q2); R-2 kept 'poor intake' (Q13).
Product issue: A medication the physician had already stopped (Vancomycin, Stopped · Oct 11) turns into 'Held · today' when the pre-round note only mentions it in passing ('level was high before we stopped it'). Separately, a dose change dictated at the visit ('Furosemide down to 20', 'Amlodipine up to 10') leaves the old dose in the row name (known B06), and on the Nursing Home visit the amlodipine increase is tagged 'Started' instead of 'Changed'.

newspec-c: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue))
Reproduced in 3 runs (no spec change after review). Device B (Honolulu, clock = server - 2 days) Save & Extract 'Hold lisinopril, BP soft.' (hold answered at the socket): stored changeDate 'Oct 11', row updatedAt and medicationsUpdatedAt 2026-10-12T07:02 (server 2026-10-14T07:02). B's screenshot 'Held · Oct 11' was taken before the server lifecycle ran; once it ran (AppLayout ContextLifecycle: whenever a page enters the Hospital section on any device, then every 10 min) it deleted the held row against its 2-day-old stamp: server medications [] and A's Medication Tracker 'No medications recorded.' Recorded only (gated TFA-94699, U20): the resident's visit date stored as B's day 'Sun Oct 11 2026'.
Product issue: A physician on a phone/laptop whose date is two days behind dictates 'Hold lisinopril, BP soft.' and taps Save & Extract: the hold is stamped 'Held · Oct 11' and, the next time the server lifecycle runs (any device entering the Hospital section, or the 10-minute timer), the lisinopril row is deleted: the Medication Tracker shows 'No medications recorded.' on every device. The tracker stamps (mergeMedEventsIntoList / useMedicationEventExtraction) use the device clock (new Date() / Date.now()). Breaks UAT 3.8 / U23 (server time; a wrong-clock device shows the same state) and TC-19 U1 (holds stay visible as open loops with their date).
